moves.note: Below stop, high beta, cut risk
Below stop, high beta, cut risk

plan: Trim QQQI to 20% to cure the concentration breach and reduce overall risk.
Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL) to zero for capital preservation.
Exit high-beta names like SMH, CRWD, and METU to further de-risk the portfolio.
Maintain core broad index exposure in SPY and QQQ.
This plan prioritizes capital preservation and reduces overall portfolio volatility.
conservative.read: This conservative approach targets around 1.5% per month, focusing on capital preservation. Expect lower drawdowns but also limited upside potential. Risk is significantly reduced by cutting leverage and high-beta names.

plan: Trim QQQI to 25% to cure the concentration breach.

Trim CRWD to 5% to manage single-name concentration.

balanced.read: This balanced approach targets around 2.5% per month, prioritizing risk-first growth. It aims for a blend of broad index and quality tech with reduced leverage. Expect moderate drawdowns and growth potential.

moves.note: Reduce broad index, shift to income
Reduce broad index, shift to income

plan: Add to QQQI, increasing income exposure to 30% for steady distributions.
Trim SPY to 10% and sell QQQ to zero, shifting away from growth-oriented broad index.
Sell all high-beta single names (SMH, CRWD, METU) to reduce volatility.
Cut all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL) to near zero for capital preservation.
This plan prioritizes low drawdown and reliable income over growth.
income.read: This income approach targets around 1% per month, focusing on parking cash for yield. It prioritizes low drawdown and reliable income. Distributions are variable and NAV can still fall in a selloff; this is not a savings account.
